What's holding your company back from its next level?

# The growth platform for _SaaS founders in public services_

We partner with founders who've built great software for the public sector and help them break through the barriers that limit growth: a small home market, technical debt, missing AI capability, or simply building alone. PubliX gives you the resources, the network and the community to scale.

[Discover your growth potential](https://publixgroup.io/#review) Confidential · No obligation · Founder to founder

[Why founders choose PubliX](https://publixgroup.io/why-publix.html)

Struggling with long sales cycles?

## Your customers are already our customers

When companies serving the same public-sector clients join the same group, something powerful happens: **cross-selling becomes natural**. Your scheduling platform is already deployed in the municipality that needs our grants management system.

Instead of competing for attention, our portfolio companies **open doors for each other**: shared customer relationships, joint marketing resources, and warm introductions that would take years to build alone.

### Shared relationships

Your products reach new customers through existing, trusted relationships in the group.

### Joint marketing

Pool resources for events, campaigns and content aimed at the same decision-makers.

### Revenue uplift

Cross-selling across the portfolio drives organic top-line growth for every company.

### Warm introductions

Skip the cold outreach. A colleague the customer already trusts makes the introduction.

Losing tenders you should be winning?

## We've run more public procurements than anyone

Public procurement is complex, bureaucratic and unforgiving. Miss a requirement, lose the deal. For a single company, each tender is a costly bet.

With multiple portfolio companies, PubliX runs **more public tenders, across more municipalities, more often** than any individual company could. That volume gives us a **structural advantage**: we know the process, we know the pitfalls, and we have dedicated resources to help you win.

Plus shared IT infrastructure, security auditing and compliance frameworks that meet the toughest public-sector standards.

-   Dedicated procurement specialists across the group
-   Shared compliance and IT security frameworks
-   Volume advantage: more tenders, more municipalities, more wins
-   Template library from hundreds of successful bids
-   Legal review and risk assessment for every submission

Worried about losing control of your company?

## We don't change what works. We build on it.

When we acquire a company, we invest in **the people and organisation that built it**, not just the product.

Every company in our group **keeps its own brand, its own office, and its own decision-making authority**. You won't become a faceless product line inside a giant.

Instead, we develop what you have already built, through shared learning, cross-company competence building, and strategic support that lets founders focus on what they do best: building great products.

-   **Your brand stays.** Your identity is part of your value.
-   **Your decision-making stays.** The roadmap remains yours.
-   **Your office stays.** You operate from where you are.
-   **Your culture stays.** We add resources, not restrictions.

"We joined PubliX to grow faster — and the first thing they told us was 'keep doing what you're doing, we're here to help.'"

— Alexander Törnqvist, Co-Founder & CEO, digiPlant

Is AI making your product obsolete?

## Embedded AI capability from day one

If you've built a successful SaaS company over the past 10 or 20 years, you already know: **AI will fundamentally change your market**. New products, new pricing, new expectations.

PubliX gives you access to **dedicated AI and technology expertise**, embedded in the group rather than bought in as consulting. We help you modernise your tech stack, automate internal processes, build AI-powered features, and develop new go-to-market strategies.

The companies that adapt fastest will win. **We want to help you be one of them.**

### AI product features

Integrate AI into your product to deliver more value and differentiate from competitors.

### Sales automation

AI-driven lead generation, qualification and outreach to accelerate your pipeline.

### Process modernisation

Automate internal workflows like support, onboarding and billing to free up your team.

### Data-driven strategy

Market intelligence, pricing optimisation and competitive analysis powered by AI.

Ready to grow beyond your home market?

## Take your product beyond the Nordics

Your product works in your home market. It could work across Europe. But international expansion requires **market knowledge, legal expertise, and localisation capabilities** that are hard to build from scratch.

PubliX already has **pan-Nordic presence** and is currently expanding into Northern Europe, the British and the DACH region. We bring market intelligence, legal frameworks, language capabilities and marketing expertise that make it possible for our companies to launch in new markets.

The European public sector is a massive, under-digitised market. We help you get there.

-   Active operations in Sweden, Finland and Denmark today
-   Market intelligence and regulatory mapping for European expansion
-   Legal expertise for new jurisdictions and public procurement
-   Localisation: language, marketing and cultural adaptation
-   International investor network through Aspira Partners

They made the move

By application · Confidential

## Discover your growth potential

We offer a select number of founders a confidential, in-depth growth assessment: a serious analysis of how your company could scale with the right resources. More markets, stronger products, AI capabilities, reduced technical debt. Every assessment is bespoke and delivered personally by our CEO.

1.  1

    #### You apply

    Tell us who you are and what your company does. We review every application personally.

2.  2

    #### We confirm fit & sign NDA

    If there's a potential fit, we set up a confidential conversation and sign a mutual NDA to protect both sides.

3.  3

    #### We map your growth potential

    New markets, product expansion, AI capabilities, technical debt reduction and competitive positioning, tailored to your company.

4.  4

    #### We present it in person

    Your assessment is delivered in a private meeting, founder to founder. The insights are yours, with no obligation and no pressure.

Are you a founder wondering what comes next?

# Why founders choose _PubliX_

You've spent years building something meaningful. We think that deserves a permanent home, not a three-year flip.

[Discover your growth potential](https://publixgroup.io/index.html#review) [See our process](https://publixgroup.io/why-publix.html#process)

Ready to scale but missing some pieces?

## You built it. We help you grow it further.

You've built a great company. You know your market, your customers and your organisation better than anyone.

What changes is what's around you. The barriers that have held you back start to disappear: a small home market, technical debt, missing AI capability, doing everything yourself. PubliX gives you the **resources, the network, and the community** to take the next step.

PubliX is a **permanent owner**, backed by Aspira Partners, who share our long-term conviction. No fund timeline, no countdown clock: your next chapter starts here.

What does joining PubliX actually mean?

## A permanent home, real AI, and shared customers

### A permanent home

No forced exits, no artificial timelines. PubliX is a permanent owner, backed by Aspira Partners, who share our long-term conviction. Your company grows at its own pace.

### AI-powered growth

Every company gets a tailored AI roadmap within 90 days. Product features, process automation, tooling: we embed capabilities your company couldn't build alone.

### Public sector DNA

We only work in one vertical. That means shared procurement expertise, shared customers, and colleagues who understand framework agreements, not just ARR.

Does it actually work?

## Results, not promises

Aspicore

ARR improvement: AI-powered grant matching drove measurable revenue growth within 6 months

Annual savings: operational automation freed resources to reinvest directly into product

What do founders who joined say?

Planning your succession?

## A new owner who backs the next generation

For many founders, the next step is a change of ownership: a founder retiring, a family deciding what happens to the company. It is a big decision, for you and for the people who built the company with you.

With PubliX, the company stays and gets broader shoulders. We support the next leader in day-to-day operations and in the strategic questions, and we bring in competence that a company your size rarely can hire on its own.

What does the process look like?

## From first call to day one in 3–5 months

No surprises, no hidden agendas. This is what happens, step by step.

### 1\. First conversation

~1 hour

A relaxed, confidential conversation between you and our leadership. No PowerPoints, no pressure. We want to understand your company, its history and what you’re thinking about. You’ll get a clear sense of who we are and how we work.

**Alexander Hübel**, CEO

**Marcus Åström**, Head of M&A

### 2\. Getting to know each other

2–4 weeks

We sign a mutual NDA and start learning about your business in more depth: financials, customers, product, team. You learn more about us. This is a two-way evaluation, and we take it seriously.

### 3\. Growth plan & indicative offer

~2 weeks

We present a tailored growth plan: how your company could scale through new markets, shared customers, AI capabilities and reduced technical debt as part of PubliX. Alongside it, you receive an indicative offer with a transparent valuation methodology. No complex structures.

### 4\. Due diligence

4–8 weeks

A structured process where we verify the details together. We use experienced advisors and keep the process respectful of your time. Most founders say this is where they realised we were different: we treat due diligence as collaboration, not interrogation.

### 5\. Welcome to PubliX

Day one

You join a group of founder-led companies building for the public good. Your brand and your office stay. What changes: you get shared AI capabilities, AI automation of internal processes, cross-selling opportunities, and colleagues who understand your market.

Still have questions?

## We believe in full transparency

### Will my company keep its own brand?

Yes. Your brand and identity are part of what makes your company valuable. We don't merge brands or fold you into a faceless group. You keep your name, your identity, and your place in the market.

### Will you change my product?

No. Product decisions stay with you and your team. We’ll offer AI capabilities, engineering support, and strategic input, but the roadmap is yours. We’re operators, not product managers.

### How long does the whole process take?

Typically 3–5 months from first conversation to close. We don’t rush, but we don’t drag things out either. The timeline depends largely on due diligence complexity and your own readiness.

### How do you value my company?

We use a transparent, market-based methodology that considers recurring revenue, growth trajectory, market position, customer quality and team strength. You’ll see the full model, with no black boxes. We present our valuation in person so you can challenge every assumption.

> "You cannot separate the technical reality of a built and maintained system from the team that built it — they have to be judged as one unit. That's why we at PubliX respect the team and the culture that created and maintained it."

Patrick Zeits

CTO, PubliX Group

## Ready for a confidential conversation?

A growth assessment is a serious, personalised analysis, not a sales pitch. It's yours to keep whether we work together or not.

About PubliX Group

# Operators building for the public good

PubliX Group unites founder-led SaaS companies that digitise public services across Northern Europe. We're operators, not financial engineers. Every decision we make starts with one question: does this help our companies build better products?

Our thesis

## Public-sector software is its own discipline

Public sector means procurement rules, framework agreements, long sales cycles and regulated buyers. It requires patience, domain expertise and a deep understanding of how the public sector actually buys technology. **PubliX concentrates in this one vertical** and intends to be the best in the Nordics. When a founder joins PubliX, they get a parent company that truly understands their market.

We grow through **shared customers and cross-selling**. Our companies sell to the same and adjacent customers: municipalities, regions, foundations, public agencies. Cross-selling and collaboration between portfolio companies grows revenue organically. Every company keeps its own brand, its identity and its autonomy.

### One vertical

100% focus on public-sector SaaS across the Nordics

### Shared customers

Municipalities, regions & foundations that buy from multiple companies

### Independent brands

Every company keeps its own brand, identity & decision-making authority

### Growth-driven

We grow revenue through cross-sell across the group

How we create value

## Two tracks. One goal: make your company stronger.

Every company we work with benefits from two parallel tracks: one strengthens your foundation, the other accelerates growth.

### Foundations

Strengthen the operational core so you can scale with confidence.

-   Clean economics: clear reporting, margins and unit economics
-   Sensible pricing: value-based models that capture what you're worth
-   Commercial discipline: pipeline management and sales processes
-   Security & compliance uplift: ISO 27001, GDPR, public-sector standards
-   AI & engineering capability: embedded tech expertise, not consultants

### Growth

Expand your market reach through the power of the platform.

-   Sell more to shared customers: cross-sell across the portfolio
-   Open new Nordic countries for proven products
-   Add adjacent workflows for the same buyer persona
-   Joint marketing & events to shared decision-makers
-   Warm introductions through trusted existing relationships

How we work with AI

## We put AI to work:  
Every product, every workflow, every job role

We embed AI across every company in the group, from new product capabilities to internal operations.

### Product AI

We help our companies build AI-powered features into their products, from intelligent automation to predictive analytics for public-sector workflows.

### Operational AI

We automate lead generation, lead nurture, customer support, software development and financial and administrative workflows across the group, so our companies can focus on building great products instead of admin.

### AI upskilling

We train every team across the group to use AI tools effectively, so capability turns into results.

> "We do everything we can together with the companies — while letting them stay independent. Collaboration is one of the most important things we do: where founders once had ten colleagues, they now have a hundred, and that collaboration continues long after they get home."

Alexander Hübel

Group CEO, PubliX Group

## Thinking about your next chapter?

Our companies

# Founder-led, mission‑driven

Every company in the PubliX portfolio was built by founders who care deeply about public services. They chose to join us and stayed to keep building.

Social care

### Tidvis

Tidvis provides an integrated business system for the social care sector: scheduling, time reporting, payroll and documentation in one platform for personal assistance and LSS providers. Their tools are designed by people who understand the daily reality of care work.

Adam Hjort

CEO

Stockholm, Sweden [tidvis.se](https://tidvis.se/)

Grant management

### digiPlant

digiPlant develops SBS Manager, an application management platform for foundations, sponsors and public organisations, from receiving applications to review, decision and disbursement. Easier applications, shorter handling times and more grants paid out.

Alexander Törnqvist

Co-Founder & CEO

Örebro, Sweden [digiplant.se](https://www.digiplant.se/sv/)

Foundation management

### Aspicore

Aspicore builds digital platforms for foundation and grant management, helping public-benefit organisations process applications, manage grants and ensure transparent governance.

Harri Tanner

CEO

Helsinki, Finland [aspicore.com](https://aspicore.com/)

Healthcare staffing

### Koivu Solutions (Sotender)

Koivu Solutions develops Sotender, a mobile-first platform that connects healthcare workers with open shifts and reduces reliance on staffing agencies. The wellbeing services county of Ostrobothnia has reported annual savings of more than EUR 7 million.

Janne Salmi

Co-Founder & CEO

Helsinki, Finland [sotender.fi](https://sotender.fi/)

Crime prevention

### Embrace Safety

Embrace Safety develops EMBRACE, a platform for knowledge-based crime prevention and safety promotion. Municipalities, police authorities and organisations use it to map situation reports, analyse causes and follow up preventive measures.

Johan Rydberg

CEO & Head of Sales

Örebro, Sweden [embracesafety.se](https://www.embrace-safety.se/)

Public communication

### Bleau

Bleau develops moliri, a compliance-driven platform for secure and accessible digital communication in the public sector, and NemBolig for Danish social housing organisations. Content is checked for accessibility, security and compliance at the point of publishing.

Robert G. Filtenborg

CEO

Aarhus, Denmark [bleau.dk](https://www.bleau.dk/)

Casework & correspondence

### Elected Technologies

Elected Technologies develops Caseworker, a casework and correspondence system for elected representatives and their offices, used in 16 parliaments around the world. CaseworkerGov does the same for councils and public bodies, and VoterID handles constituency and membership management for MPs and political parties.

Simon McIntyre

Founder & CEO

Shipston-on-Stour, UK [electedtechnologies.com](https://www.electedtechnologies.com/)

> "Right from our first contact, we felt a strong trust in the buyer. They treated us with respect, asked thoughtful, sensible questions and really listened to our answers. We also felt that PubliX offered a structure — a group of companies that all contribute to societal value."

Johan Rydberg

CEO, Embrace Safety

Post-acquisition

## What happens after you join

Joining PubliX is designed to be straightforward. This is what the first year looks like for a typical portfolio company.

1

### Day one: Nothing changes

Your team, your office, your customers. We're not here to reorganise.

2

### Months 1–3: Foundations

We work together on economics, pricing, compliance and security.

3

### Months 3–12: Growth

Cross-sell to shared customers, open new countries, add adjacent workflows.

4

### Year 1+: Platform value

Share in the collective growth of the group. Your success compounds.

News

# What's happening at PubliX

Acquisitions, partnerships and milestones from PubliX Group and the companies in the portfolio.

All Acquisitions Appointments Milestones

November 24, 2026 Acquisition

## PubliX Group acquires Elected Technologies and enters the UK

Elected Technologies, maker of Caseworker, becomes the seventh company in PubliX Group and its first outside the Nordics. Simon McIntyre stays on as CEO.

[Read more](https://publixgroup.io/news/elected-technologies.html)

September 10, 2026 Acquisition

## PubliX Group acquires Bleau A/S and enters the Danish market

Bleau, the Aarhus company behind moliri, becomes the sixth company in PubliX Group and its first in Denmark. It keeps its name and its management.

[Read more](https://publixgroup.io/news/bleau.html)

April 14, 2026 Appointment

## PubliX Group appoints Alexander Hübel as CEO

title: "PubliX Group acquires Elected Technologies, maker of Caseworker, and enters the UK"
description: "Elected Technologies, whose Caseworker system is used in 16 parliaments, becomes the seventh company in PubliX Group and its first outside the Nordics. Simon McIntyre stays on as CEO."
url: https://publixgroup.io/news/elected-technologies.html

---

November 24, 2026 Acquisition

# PubliX Group acquires Elected Technologies, maker of Caseworker, and enters the UK

Elected Technologies, the Warwickshire company whose Caseworker system is used in 16 parliaments around the world, becomes the seventh company in PubliX Group and its first outside the Nordics. Its founder, Simon McIntyre, stays on as CEO.

PubliX Group has acquired Elected Technologies Ltd, which develops Caseworker, a casework and correspondence system for elected representatives and the government sector. Elected is the group's seventh company and its first outside the Nordics. It follows Bleau A/S of Aarhus, which joined on 31 August, and PubliX now has companies in four countries: three in Sweden, two in Finland, one in Denmark and one in the UK.

Elected is based in South Warwickshire and has teams in Adelaide, Australia, and Ottawa, Canada. Its primary product, Caseworker, brings an organisation's emails, letters and tasks into one place, providing tracking and a full picture of the interactions between a citizen and those who represent and serve them. Caseworker and VoterID are already used by representatives in 16 parliaments around the world, while CaseworkerGov does the same for councils and public bodies, including support for freedom of information requests and other voice-of-the-customer processes.

Elected Technologies' software supports busy offices and organisations that often operate with limited resources. The new Case Assist and AI Triage features pick out names and addresses from incoming correspondence, and prioritise, summarise, categorise and tag each case automatically. The user still decides what happens next, but the AI tools suggest actions based on the way each client operates, with a human always in the loop.

For the people who work at Elected, the company keeps its name, its CEO and its offices, and PubliX will not merge it with its existing businesses. Customers keep their existing agreements, including terms on how and where their data is held and processed, and Elected remains a non-partisan platform in the elected representative space.

Simon McIntyre, founder and CEO of Elected Technologies

“Over the last 11 years Elected has achieved fantastic growth, but I still feel there’s a lot more to come and I’m excited to continue to lead that. PubliX is going to be a fantastic home for us and will deliver exactly what we need as we navigate the second decade of our growth journey,” said Simon McIntyre, CEO and founder of Elected Technologies.

“In PubliX I have people to talk to who are in the same position as me. Once a month I’ll meet the other CEOs in the group, and both I and the rest of my team are gaining access to the group’s specialists and experts. I really believe that working together we’ll be more than the sum of our parts. We can draw on what they’ve already learned and share our own expertise and knowledge back. Ultimately that’s great for all our customers, and will mean our products, that so many people rely on, can improve at an even faster rate.”

“We chose Elected for the work its software does. The cases that reach an MP’s office are personal, about housing, health, benefits or immigration, and Caseworker is built to keep track of each one. Two acquisitions since August have taken us from two countries to four, and we intend to build further in the UK, including through acquisitions in fields close to Elected’s. I expect the people who use Caseworker, CaseworkerGov and VoterID to see the difference in how quickly the products develop,” said Alexander Hübel, Group CEO of PubliX Group.

The group's central team will work with Elected on AI, public-sector sales and procurement, and support it with its existing IT security and compliance processes. Elected also gains six sister companies: fellow software businesses serving public services in Sweden, Finland and Denmark.

PubliX Group continues to look for founder-led software companies in Northern Europe that serve the public sector, with the current focus on the Nordics, the UK, and Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

### About Elected Technologies

Elected Technologies Ltd is a UK software company founded in 2014 and based in Shipston-on-Stour, Warwickshire. It develops Caseworker, a casework and correspondence system for elected representatives and their offices, CaseworkerGov for councils and public bodies, and VoterID, a constituency and membership management system for MPs and political parties. Its products are used in 16 parliaments worldwide.

title: "PubliX Group enters Denmark and welcomes Bleau A/S"
description: "Bleau, the Danish company behind moliri, becomes the sixth company in PubliX Group and its first in Denmark. Same name, same team, same product plan."
url: https://publixgroup.io/news/bleau.html
language: en
---

September 10, 2026 Acquisition

# PubliX Group enters Denmark and welcomes Bleau A/S

Bleau is the Danish company behind moliri, the platform municipalities use to publish information citizens can actually use.

A municipality's website is where people renew a permit, find a school place, or read what to do when the water is off. Every page has to be right and readable by everyone, including people who use a screen reader, and the text comes from across the organisation, written by people whose job is care, planning or waste collection. moliri checks the page as it is written, before it is published.

22 of Denmark's 98 municipalities publish their citizen information through moliri, and 35 social housing organisations use the NemBolig version to reach residents. Utilities and transport operators use it too. Bleau has been building for these buyers since 2008.

Bleau is our sixth company and our first in Denmark, alongside three in Sweden and two in Finland. Bleau stays Bleau: same name, same team, same product plan, and customers keep the agreements they have. Robert Filtenborg continues as CEO and Peter Terkildsen as CTO. PubliX adds capital to grow with, and group support on international growth, public procurement, security and compliance, pricing and AI.

"Denmark has been on our list since we set the acquisition strategy, and Bleau is the company I really wanted in it," said Alexander Hübel, Group CEO of PubliX Group. "Robert and Peter have built a business that municipalities trust with their most important communication. That is what we are buying, and something we certainly intend to preserve — and grow."

"By choosing PubliX Group we have made sure that Bleau remains Bleau," said Robert Filtenborg, CEO of Bleau A/S. "Our strategy and development plans for moliri are unchanged. The difference is that we now have greater strength to grow, nationally and internationally."

### About Bleau A/S

Bleau A/S is a Danish software company founded in Aarhus in 2008. Bleau develops moliri, a compliance-driven SaaS platform for digital communication in the public sector, and NemBolig, a platform for Danish social housing organisations.

title: "Sotender launches in Sweden: Suomikoti is first customer"
description: "Finnish SaaS platform Sotender enters the Swedish market. Suomikoti, a Finnish-speaking care home in Enskede with 53 residents, becomes the first Swedish customer."
url: https://publixgroup.io/news/sotender-launches-sweden-suomikoti.html
language: en
---

May 4, 2026 Milestone

# Sotender launches in Sweden: Suomikoti is first customer

Finnish SaaS company Koivu Solutions brings its substitute-staffing platform Sotender to the Swedish market. Its first customer is Suomikoti, a Finnish-speaking care and residential home in Enskede, Stockholm, with 53 places serving elderly care and dementia care.

Sotender is built to reduce the time and uncertainty involved in filling short-notice shifts and to strengthen an organisation's ability to handle unplanned absence. The platform replaces phone calls and text messages with a few clicks in a shared substitute-staffing system.

## Clear impact in daily operations

At Suomikoti, staffing was previously handled mainly by phone and text, an approach that often led to delays and heavy workload in urgent situations.

"Finding substitutes used to be stressful. Needs come up quickly and it was hard to reach the right people. Now it only takes one click to publish a shift," says HR assistant Anu Tuomenharju.

"I posted several shifts in Sotender and could then focus on other work. When I checked again later, almost all of them were already filled. We don't have to call around anymore," she says.

The majority of Suomikoti's staff use the system today, and feedback has been predominantly positive after an initial onboarding phase.

## Significant time and cost savings

Sotender is already well established in Finland, with more than 40,000 users and around 20 customer organisations, including 11 wellbeing services counties (välfärdsområden), according to Anna Aubert, Head of Sales and Marketing at Koivu Solutions. The Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county has publicly stated that it saves more than EUR 7 million per year using the solution.

The platform is aimed at organisations where absence is part of everyday life, such as elderly care, hospitals, home care and preschools.

"Across our Finnish wellbeing services counties we see that time spent on substitute-staffing can be cut in half or more, while dependence on staffing agencies decreases," says Chief Architect Teemu Santala.

## Continued expansion in Sweden

The Swedish launch marks the next step in the company's international expansion. Koivu Solutions is now seeking additional customers in Sweden.

"We want to give managers in health and social care a tool that frees up time and lowers costs. Interest from Sweden is strong and we are in dialogue with several parties," says Eero Puikkonen, Sweden Lead at Koivu Solutions.

### About Koivu Solutions

Koivu Solutions is a Finnish SaaS company developing digital solutions for efficient substitute staffing in health, social care and education. Its Sotender platform is used today by more than 40,000 employees across around 20 customer organisations in Finland, including 11 wellbeing services counties. Koivu Solutions is part of PubliX Group AB.

### About Suomikoti

Suomikoti is a Finnish-speaking care and residential home in Enskede, Stockholm, offering accommodation for elderly with somatic diagnoses and dementia. Founded in 1995, the non-profit association operates 53 apartments with a high share of trained staff specialised in dementia care.

### Contact

Eero Puikkonen  
Sweden Lead, Koivu Solutions Oy (Sotender)  
[eero.puikkonen@koivusolutions.com](mailto:eero.puikkonen@koivusolutions.com)  
[www.sotender.io](https://www.sotender.io/)

April 14, 2026 Appointment

# PubliX Group appoints Alexander Hübel as CEO

Alexander Hübel has been appointed Group CEO of PubliX Group, bringing extensive experience in scaling technology companies and building platforms in the Nordic market.

STOCKHOLM — PubliX Group has appointed Alexander Hübel as Group CEO. He takes over from Marcus Åström, who has led the group as acting CEO since its formation and continues in his role as Head of M&A.

Alexander Hübel brings roughly a decade of work with AI at scale: at Ericsson he built and led large, complex organisations; at Turbotic he played a central role in developing and scaling AI-driven products globally; and as COO of DigitalTolk he drove AI innovation and international expansion.

At the time of the appointment, PubliX Group comprised five founder-led software companies across Sweden and Finland, serving municipalities, healthcare and social care, foundations and public authorities. A central part of Hübel's mandate is to put AI to work across the portfolio, automating routine work while keeping people accountable for what reaches the citizen.

Patrik Sallner remains chairman of the board. The group, backed by Aspira Partners, continues to look for founder-led software companies in the Nordics that run regulated public-sector workflows.

### About PubliX Group

We acquire and develop vertical software companies providing essential solutions to the public sector in Northern Europe.

March 5, 2026 Acquisition

# PubliX Group partners with Embrace Safety

A powerful SaaS platform enabling knowledge-based crime prevention and safety promotion for municipalities and local authorities.

STOCKHOLM, 5 March 2026 — PubliX Group partners with Embrace Safety, whose platform EMBRACE enables knowledge-based crime prevention and safety promotion for municipalities and local authorities. Embrace Safety was founded in Örebro in 2018 by Henrik Andershed, professor of criminology at Örebro University, and is led by CEO Johan Rydberg.

EMBRACE combines analytical software with continuous knowledge support: municipalities, police authorities and organisations use it to map and share situation reports on crime and insecurity, analyse causes, and document and follow up preventive measures. Several hundred organisations use the platform today.

Demand is driven by law: since 2023, Swedish municipalities have a statutory responsibility for crime prevention work under lag (2023:196), including producing recurring situation reports, exactly the workflow EMBRACE supports.

"Right from our first contact, we felt a strong trust in the buyer. They treated us with respect, asked thoughtful, sensible questions and really listened to our answers. We also felt that PubliX offered a structure — a group of companies that all contribute to societal value," said Johan Rydberg, CEO of Embrace Safety.

Embrace Safety continues under its own brand with its own team, and gains sister companies with standing relationships across Nordic public-sector markets.

### About Embrace Safety

Embrace Safety is a Swedish SaaS company founded in Örebro in 2018. Its platform EMBRACE supports knowledge-based crime prevention and safety promotion for municipalities, police authorities and organisations.

December 16, 2025 Acquisition

# PubliX Group partners with Koivu Solutions (Sotender)

A modern SaaS solution for connecting healthcare workers with open shifts, increasing reach and reducing costs for healthcare providers.

HELSINKI, 16 December 2025 — PubliX Group has acquired 100 per cent of the shares in Koivu Solutions Oy, the Finnish company behind Sotender, a mobile-first platform that connects healthcare workers with open shifts and reduces reliance on staffing agencies. At the time of the announcement, Sotender had more than 27,000 users in Finland, with its first Swedish implementation underway.

The results are public: the wellbeing services county of Ostrobothnia has reported annual savings of more than EUR 7 million, with 96.7 per cent of open shifts booked through Sotender.

"This partnership strengthens Koivu without changing who we are. Our team, our mission, and our customer relationships will remain the same," said Janne Salmi, CEO and co-founder of Koivu Solutions.

"Koivu embodies the type of specialized, mission-driven SaaS company we want in the PubliX Group," said Marcus Åström, interim CEO and Head of M&A at PubliX Group.

Koivu Solutions, founded in 2017, continues as an independent company within the group: same team, same brand. The current owners continue in operational roles and reinvest a significant portion of the proceeds to become PubliX shareholders.

### About Koivu Solutions

Koivu Solutions is a Finnish SaaS company founded in 2017. Its platform Sotender connects healthcare workers with open shifts, reducing reliance on staffing agencies across Finnish wellbeing services counties.

# PubliX Group enters Finland through partnership with Aspicore

A full-service software provider within grant management, marking PubliX Group's expansion into the Finnish market.

STOCKHOLM, 2 September 2025 — PubliX Group enters Finland through a partnership with Aspicore, a full-service software provider within grant management. Aspicore's cloud platform Apuraha4 supports foundations, organisations, unions, universities and public authorities through the complete lifecycle of grants, from application to payment.

Aspicore, led by CEO Harri Tanner, builds on two decades of work with grant systems. Apuraha4 is used by 140 customer organisations, which together manage more than EUR 100 million in grants annually.

The partnership marks PubliX Group's first step outside Sweden. Together with digiPlant, Aspicore forms the basis of a leading pan-Nordic challenger within grant management software.

### About Aspicore

Aspicore is a Finnish full-service software provider within grant management. Its platform Apuraha4 is used by 140 customer organisations, managing more than EUR 100 million in grants annually.

August 25, 2025 Acquisition

# PubliX Group partners with digiPlant

A market leader within application management systems for foundations, strengthening PubliX's position in the grant management vertical.

STOCKHOLM, 25 August 2025 — PubliX Group has entered a partnership with digiPlant, a market leader within application management systems for foundations. digiPlant, founded in Örebro in 2000, develops SBS Manager, a platform that manages the complete case flow of grant-making organisations, from receiving applications and communicating with applicants to review, decision, budgeting and disbursement.

The societal case is concrete: applications become easier and more accessible for applicants, handling processes are drastically shortened, more grants are paid out and fraudulent behaviour is reduced. Adolf Lindgrens Stiftelse, one of digiPlant's customers, quadrupled its number of applications after moving to SBS Manager.

digiPlant is led by CEO Alexander Törnqvist and has held a AAA credit rating from Dun & Bradstreet for ten consecutive years.

digiPlant is PubliX Group's second partnership, following the acquisition of Tidvis earlier the same month, and continues under its own brand with its own team.

### About digiPlant

digiPlant is a Swedish software company founded in Örebro in 2000. Its platform SBS Manager handles the complete application and case management flow for foundations, sponsors and public organisations.

August 25, 2025 Acquisition

# PubliX Group welcomes Tidvis

Strengthening digital care solutions in the Nordics: Tidvis develops platforms for social services, helping municipalities manage case work and compliance.

STOCKHOLM, 25 August 2025 — PubliX Group has acquired Tidvis, its first portfolio company. Tidvis, founded in 2012, provides an integrated business system for the Swedish social care sector, serving personal assistance providers and organisations working under LSS.

The platform gathers the daily operations of a care provider in one system: scheduling, time reporting, payroll, documentation, CRM, quality management and recruitment. It holds around 25 per cent of Sweden's private personal assistance market.

"Joining Aspira Partners and its PubliX Group marks an exciting new chapter for Tidvis. With its focus on public services SaaS solutions, PubliX will provide a strong foundation for accelerating our growth and continuing to deliver high-quality services. I am confident that this partnership will create new opportunities and benefits for both our team and our customers," said Mattias Lind, founder and CEO of Tidvis.

Tidvis continues under its own brand and with its own team. PubliX Group works as an accelerator rather than a holding company: each company keeps its identity while gaining group support in areas such as public procurement, compliance and AI.

Oaklins Sweden acted as sole financial advisor to Tidvis' owners in the transaction.

### About Tidvis

Tidvis is a Swedish SaaS company founded in 2012. Its platform integrates scheduling, time reporting, payroll and documentation for personal assistance and LSS providers, and holds around 25 per cent of Sweden's private personal assistance market.

[View all companies](https://publixgroup.io/companies.html)
